title: Wasm Fastmath Extension Algebra
objective: Close word-extension and arbitrary-prime polynomial Wasm resource execution with exact public workflows, lifecycle/memory proofs, and no silent expensive fallback

exceptions: Host-neutral FLINT resource declarations and representation headers are required to expose mature finite-field algorithms without duplicating mathematics; handwritten code is limited to checked ownership and transfer adapters.

handoff.summary: Enabled receipt-backed fq_context, fq_element, and fq_polynomial resources plus 27 pointer-free FLINT functions in the production WebAssembly closure. Added real-artifact exact arithmetic, cross-context ownership, deterministic cleanup, memory-growth, and 127-bit arbitrary-prime polynomial witnesses. The generated extension-field source wrappers now report the precise ownership-domain adapter boundary instead of a missing Wasm declaration.
risks: fq_element_coordinate and fq_polynomial_coordinate remain native-only because the generated Wasm adapter does not safely marshal nullable returned pointers; the production API uses copied bulk-coordinate byte transfers instead.

Seven extension-field source wrappers and the arbitrary-prime source wrapper still require a same-module foreign-resource ownership bridge before they can enter the production source-kernel closure, although their mature low-level FLINT resource operations now execute in real Wasm.
The public GF(p^n) parent has not yet been migrated onto these generated resources, so this lane closes the production FFI substrate rather than claiming end-to-end public parent dispatch.
The eager raw artifact is now 6.24 MiB and its JavaScript backend is about 364 KiB, within the reviewed raised budgets but still worth integration payload review.
next_steps: Migrate the public finite-field and polynomial parents to the generated fq resource substrate with exact differential and lifecycle tests.
Generate a same-module source-to-resource ownership bridge, or retire the redundant source wrappers from the production registry in favor of the generated batch resource ABI.
Evaluate whether the fq closure should remain eager or move behind a lazy module boundary based on compressed payload and startup measurements.
